aria: Animated recap of the Trail Blazers' 124 to 114 win at Milwaukee: Damian Lillard's 3-pointer with 4:12 left that made it 115 to 110, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his season-high 33 points in his return to Milwaukee, the top scorers, how Portland won, and Saturday's game at New York.
notes: Box score from the Trail Blazers' 124–114 win over the Milwaukee Bucks in Milwaukee on Nov 19, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, line score and team stats, checked against the CBS Sports box score (final score, line score, records, team totals). All 124 Portland points and all 114 Milwaukee points are accounted for in the player lines, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Portland 24–21 after one, 60–58 at the half, 96–92 after three, 28–22 in the fourth. Team stats (field goals 41 of 77, 53.2%, to 40 of 91, 44.0%; threes 17 of 43 to 16 of 41; free throws 25 of 32 to 18 of 26; defensive rebounds 36–23; offensive rebounds 9–12; blocks 5–1; steals 12–14; biggest lead Portland 12, Milwaukee 8) are from Covers and CBS. One outlet (SI) lists Lillard with four threes; the box score and the AP-style recaps give five. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Thursday's games.

Lillard's 33 was a season high in his first game in Milwaukee since the Bucks waived him (AP; KNBR). Scoot Henderson scored a season-high 27 with 5 of 6 from three (KATU; AP); Jrue Holiday scored 13 of his 22 in the fourth quarter (KNBR); Toumani Camara scored all 18 after halftime, with four threes in a 19–2 third-quarter run (KNBR; AP). Portland led 60–58 at the half (KNBR). Brayden Burries' three gave Milwaukee a 108–106 lead with 5:48 left (KNBR; Heavy); Holiday's two baskets put Portland up 112–108 with 4:44 left (KNBR); Tyler Herro's driving basket cut it to 115–114 with 3:18 left, and Portland scored the game's last nine points (AP; Heavy), the last two on Lillard free throws (Yahoo Sports). The game had 20 lead changes and eight ties (AP). Milwaukee has lost 12 straight, its longest skid since a 15-game run in March 1996, and is 1–15, its worst start through 16 games (AP). It was Portland's sixth straight win over Milwaukee (KNBR; Heavy). Saturday's game is Portland's only visit to Madison Square Garden this season (KATU). Deni Avdija missed a second straight game with a sore left foot; Milwaukee was without Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Damian Lillard's 3-pointer with 4:12 left that made it 115–110, the end of a 9–2 Portland run after Milwaukee led by two (clock, shot and score from KATU; the 108–106 and 112–108 scores before it from KNBR and Heavy, and the 115–114 score after it from AP). The written accounts don't describe how the shot was created, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up, not the exact move. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Portland Trail Blazers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Lillard's listed 6-foot-2 and 200 pounds (Basketball-Reference 2026-27 roster; Yahoo Sports), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-7.75 wingspan at the 2012 draft combine (NBADraft.net, as in earlier Portland recaps), in the Blazers' road red with No. 0 (Basketball-Reference) and his proposed look. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
